takeaway: A pinch holds only if each finger pushes within a narrow cone set by friction; tilt the grip outside the cones and the object slides out.

selfCheck.question: Why do grippers have rubber pads?
selfCheck.answer: rubber is grippy, wider cone (45 vs 17 vs 6); can hold when tilted or not lined up; room to spare.

sentence: A fingertip can only push on an object within a certain range of angles before it slides off, and that range is shown as a cone. When a gripper squeezes at a tilt, the block stays put only if the slant still fits inside both fingertips' cones. Slippery surfaces make the cones narrower, so a tilted grip that works on rubber can fail on plastic or ice.
